entry.title: I Built a Global Opinion Platform in 72 Hours — Here Is What Actually Went Wrong
entry.summary:
I finished the Groundswell hackathon build with a working product, a deployed URL, and a list of things I wish I had known before I started. This is that list. Not the polished version where everything went according to plan — the actual version, including the three hours I spent debugging a database connection that was failing for a reason I had completely wrong. Mistake 1 — Assuming Aurora DSQL Works Like Regular PostgreSQL Mistake 2 — Planning for Tables That Did Not Exist Yet Mistake 3 — Underestimating How Different Concurrent Writes and Relational Reads Actually Are What Actually Surprised Me in a Good Way The Bedrock integration for question generation was simpler than I expected. A prompt describing the type of question I needed, a structured JSON format for the response, and some string parsing to remove the markdown wrappers the model adds around its output. The model returns five candidate questions with predicted divergence scores. An admin reviews and approves one before it goes live. The whole thing works reliably. The Vercel Marketplace provisioning for both databases genuinely took minutes. Environment variables were injected automatically. The infrastructure was ready before I finished reading the documentation. I created this content as part of entering the H0: Hack the Zero Stack hackathon. The mistakes were expensive in time during the build. They were worth it for what they taught. tags: aws, dynamodb, nextjs, hackathon, webdev

entry.title: Building "Focus Flow" — A Serverless Productivity Suite with AWS Aurora and Vercel v0
entry.summary:
Disclaimer: I created this post and project for the purposes of entering the H0: Hack the Zero Stack with Vercel v0 and AWS Databases hackathon. We all juggle daily tasks, shared groceries, personal debts, and monthly expenses. But managing them usually means jumping between five different apps. It’s chaotic, and it's inefficient. For the #H0Hackathon, I built Focus Flow — a unified productivity suite that brings your daily logistics into one beautiful, centralized dashboard. Here is how I built a highly responsive, AI-powered platform over a weekend using a zero-trust serverless architecture. Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router) & Tailwind CSS UI Scaffolding: Vercel v0 Database: AWS Aurora PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM AI Engine: Amazon Bedrock (Nova Lite model) Deployment: Vercel One of the biggest hurdles when building cloud-connected productivity apps is latency. Waiting for a round-trip database operation to an AWS Aurora instance can introduce micro-delays that ruin a user's sense of flow. I solved this by diving deep into Next.js Server Actions and implementing aggressive optimistic UI updates on the client components. When a user adds a high-priority task or logs an expense, the interface updates instantly with zero latency, while securely synchronizing relational integrity with Aurora in the background. Instead of just showing static rows of numbers, Focus Flow acts as an active assistant. I integrated Amazon Bedrock natively using the Amazon Nova Lite model. It evaluates raw expense entries and synthesizes them into cohesive, personalized financial outlooks on the fly. Building a fully serverless, production-ready stack in such a compressed timeframe felt like assembling a complex puzzle, but seeing it run with zero latency was incredibly rewarding. 📺 Watch the Demo: https://youtu.be/kgREBZmZZjs
💻 GitHub Repo: https://github.com/Jerinbabujb/focus-flow-next
🌐 Live App: https://focus-flow-six-chi.vercel.app/auth

entry.title: Why Most People Never Discover Their Real Potential
entry.summary:
Every year, millions of people choose careers based on expectations, salaries, or what seems like the "safe" option. Yet many eventually realize they're working in roles that don't align with who they truly are. The problem isn't a lack of intelligence or ambition—it's a lack of self-understanding. Traditional personality tests have helped many people, but they often produce static reports based on a fixed set of questions. Real people are far more complex. Our strengths evolve with experience, and understanding them requires more than a multiple-choice quiz. Recent advances in artificial intelligence open the door to a different approach. Instead of generating a one-time report, AI can have conversations, ask follow-up questions, recognize patterns, and provide personalized insights that adapt over time. This idea is what inspired me to start building PotenAI. The goal isn't to replace human judgment or career coaches. The goal is to give people another tool—one that helps them better understand their strengths, hidden talents, career fit, and long-term potential. We're currently building the first version, and there's still a long journey ahead. But I genuinely believe AI can make self-discovery more accessible and more personal than ever before. I'm curious to hear your thoughts. Do you think AI can help people understand themselves better than traditional assessments?

entry.title: How Uniswap Scales Across Every Chain with Quicknode
entry.summary: Uniswap products feel the same on every chain. Here's how Uniswap Labs scales across 19+ networks, and the multi-chain RPC infrastructure Quicknode runs underneath to make launch day work.
